name: Ketovore
summary: Keto with a meat-first bias and a few plants allowed; a hybrid label with no trials of its own.
lead: Ketovore is an informal label for a diet that combines ketogenic, very low-carbohydrate eating with a meat-heavy emphasis, while still allowing some plant foods. It sits between a standard ketogenic diet and the carnivore diet, which allows only animal products .

name: Eat like a bodybuilder (rice/chicken/broccoli)
summary: The classic bro diet: lean protein, rice and greens, built on calorie control rather than any special food.
lead: Eating like a bodybuilder, often shorthand for plain rice, chicken breast and broccoli, is a long-standing fitness diet built around high protein, measured carbohydrate and low added fat. It is used in appearance communities to gain muscle or lose fat while keeping food choices simple.

name: Meal prep
summary: Cook ahead, portion it out; a habit tool for hitting diet targets, with small studies linking it to better habits.
lead: Meal prep is the practice of planning and cooking meals in advance, often a week at a time, and storing them in portioned containers . In fitness and appearance communities it is used to control calories and protein and to avoid unplanned eating.

name: Hot-sauce thermogenics / spicy food
summary: Spicy food as a metabolism booster; capsaicin may nudge appetite slightly, but weight-loss evidence is weak.
lead: Hot-sauce thermogenics refers to eating chili peppers, hot sauce or capsaicin supplements in the belief that the heat speeds metabolism and helps fat loss. Capsaicin, the pungent compound in chilies, binds the TRPV1 receptor on pain-sensing nerves, producing sensations of heat .

name: Sea moss / chlorella / spirulina
summary: Algae powders and gels marketed as superfood skin-and-energy boosters, with no appearance trials behind them.
lead: Sea moss, chlorella and spirulina are algae-based products sold as dietary supplements and 'superfoods'. Sea moss usually refers to Irish moss (Chondrus crispus), a red seaweed of North Atlantic coasts rich in the thickener carrageenan . Chlorella is a genus of single-celled green algae , and spirulina is the dried biomass of cyanobacteria, mainly of the genus Arthrospira .

name: Greens powders (AG1)
summary: A heavily podcast-marketed daily greens drink whose supporting trials are small and whose appearance effects are untested.
lead: Greens powders are powdered blends of vegetables, algae, herbs, vitamins and minerals mixed into water as a daily supplement. The best-known brand is AG1, formerly Athletic Greens, a Nevada-based company founded in December 2010 by Chris Ashenden that sells a roughly 75-ingredient powder by subscription .

name: Tapeworm / sanitized parasite diet
summary: Fringe idea of swallowing a parasite to lose weight; untested, and parasitic infection carries serious documented risks.
lead: The tapeworm or 'sanitized parasite' diet refers to the idea of deliberately ingesting a tapeworm, or a product claimed to contain one, in order to lose weight. It is discussed as a fringe weight-loss method, not an accepted medical treatment.

name: Chewing and spitting
summary: An eating-disorder behaviour studied in clinics as a marker of severity, not a researched appearance method.
lead: Chewing and spitting is a behaviour in which a person chews food for taste and then spits it out without swallowing. In clinical literature it is described as a compensatory or purging-type behaviour seen in people with eating disorders.

name: Extended fasting 'dopamine fasts'
summary: Abstaining from food or stimulation to 'reset'; the behavioural version is loosely defined and extended fasting carries real medical risks.
lead: This entry covers two separate practices: prolonged food fasting (going beyond 24 hours without eating, often 5 to 20 days) and 'dopamine fasting', in which a person abstains from stimulating behaviours such as phone use, gaming or pornography .

name: Alkaline water / alkaline diet
summary: Diet and water pH claims that dietitians and cancer charities say do not change blood pH; no appearance studies exist.
lead: The alkaline diet is a group of loosely related diets based on the idea that foods change the body's pH and that this affects disease. It favours most fruit and vegetables and excludes most grains, meat, cheese and eggs. Alkaline water, often made with ionizer machines, is marketed on a similar premise .

name: Detox teas / juice cleanses
summary: Teas and cleanses sold to flush out 'toxins'; reviews find no good evidence they do.
lead: Detox teas and juice cleanses are consumer products and short-term diets marketed as ways to remove unspecified "toxins" from the body. They are part of the wider alternative-medicine category of detoxification, which also includes fasting, colon cleansing and restricted diets . In appearance-focused communities they are discussed mainly in connection with clearer skin, a leaner face and reduced bloating.

name: Fruit juice cleanse
summary: A days-long juice-only diet sold as a reset; no published research backs the detox or skin claims.
lead: A fruit juice cleanse, also called juice fasting or juice cleansing, is a short-term diet, usually one to seven days, in which a person drinks only fruit and vegetable juices and eats no solid food . It is promoted as a way to detoxify the body and is treated as a form of detox diet .

name: Cold-pressed oils / olive oil
summary: Mechanically extracted oils, chiefly olive, promoted as a seed-oil swap; heart-health claims are regulator-qualified, appearance effects untested.
lead: Cold-pressed oils, most prominently extra virgin olive oil, are edible oils extracted mechanically without heat or chemical solvents. In looksmaxxing and wider diet-culture discussion they are promoted as replacements for refined seed oils, with claims about skin and general health .

name: Butter / ghee
summary: Dairy fats promoted over vegetable oils; guidelines advise limiting them for saturated fat, appearance effects untested.
lead: Butter is a dairy fat made by churning cream, about 80 percent butterfat, and ghee is a South Asian clarified butter simmered until its milk solids are removed . In looksmaxxing and ancestral-diet communities they are promoted as alternatives to vegetable oils.

name: Grass-fed beef / ethical-sourcing
summary: Pasture-raised beef touted for more omega-3 and CLA; differences exist but appearance benefits are unstudied.
lead: Grass-fed beef comes from cattle reared mainly on forage rather than grain-based finishing feed. It is promoted in diet and looksmaxxing circles for nutrient density and ethical sourcing .

name: Sardines / oily fish
summary: Cheap oily fish with B12 and omega-3; skin benefits are claimed but untested in the sources reviewed.
lead: Sardines are small, oily forage fish eaten fresh, grilled, smoked or canned. In appearance-focused diet discussion they are promoted as a source of omega-3 fatty acids said to benefit skin .

name: Eggs (egg yolk)
summary: A staple protein-and-choline food; its appearance relevance is mostly indirect.
lead: Whole eggs and egg yolks are a common food in bodybuilding and general nutrition, and are discussed in appearance-focused communities mainly as sources of protein, fat and choline. A hard-boiled chicken egg provides roughly 12.6 g of protein and 294 mg of choline per 100 g, and egg protein scores the maximum on the PDCAAS protein-quality scale.

name: Oats / rice-and-chicken carbs for bulking
summary: The cheap carb-and-chicken staple diet for a calorie-surplus bulk.
lead: A "standard bulk" built around oats, rice and chicken refers to eating in a calorie surplus using inexpensive carbohydrate and lean-protein staples in order to gain muscle. Bulking in general means eating above maintenance energy needs, and Wikipedia reports a well-established link between positive energy balance and muscle growth.

name: Sweet potato / carb timing
summary: Scheduling carbs like sweet potato around workouts; the timing effect itself is debated.
lead: Carbohydrate timing refers to the idea that when carbohydrates are eaten around training affects performance and recovery. Wikipedia describes nutrient timing as coordinating intake with exercise, with claims that carbohydrates during and after workouts help replace muscle glycogen.

name: Eating disorder-adjacent restriction ('thinspo' leanness)
summary: Extreme restriction for a gaunt look, closely tied to eating disorder content.
lead: Thinspiration ("thinspo") is imagery and content of thin people, associated with pro-ana (pro-anorexia) online communities that promote behaviours linked to anorexia nervosa. In looksmaxxing contexts, extreme restriction to reach a lean or gaunt look is sometimes discussed, and medical groups regard restrictive eating of this kind as carrying eating disorder risk.

name: Pre-workout / stim stacks
summary: High-caffeine pre-workout blends for gym energy, with mixed evidence beyond caffeine.
lead: Pre-workout supplements are products taken before training to boost energy, focus and endurance, usually containing caffeine along with ingredients such as beta-alanine, citrulline and creatine. They are sold as powders, capsules and drinks, often as proprietary blends, and the category is lightly regulated.

name: Body dysmorphic disorder (BDD)
summary: A recognised psychiatric disorder of fixation on perceived flaws, treated with CBT and SSRIs.
lead: Body dysmorphic disorder (BDD) is a mental disorder defined by an overwhelming preoccupation with a perceived flaw in physical appearance that is minor or not observable to others, causing distress and impairment. It was moved to the obsessive-compulsive spectrum in the DSM-5 in 2013, and it includes a muscle dysmorphia subtype.

name: CBT for BDD
summary: The best-studied talk therapy for body dysmorphic disorder, built around exposure and response prevention.
lead: Cognitive-behavioral therapy for body dysmorphic disorder (CBT-BDD) is a form of psychotherapy designed for people with body dysmorphic disorder (BDD), a condition marked by preoccupation with a perceived flaw in appearance. Treatment typically combines psychoeducation, cognitive restructuring, exposure with response prevention (ERP), and in some programs mindfulness and perceptual retraining.

name: SSRIs for BDD
summary: Antidepressants used for body dysmorphic disorder, a medical treatment rather than a looks tool.
lead: Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) are antidepressants that block the serotonin transporter, increasing serotonin availability in the synapse. They are among the medications used in treating body dysmorphic disorder (BDD), a condition involving preoccupation with a perceived flaw in appearance. Wikipedia's BDD article describes SSRIs and cognitive-behavioral therapy as effective treatments, and suggests SSRIs may ease obsessive-compulsive and delusional features.

name: Mirror checking / mirror avoidance
summary: Compulsive mirror checking or avoidance, behaviors described in body dysmorphic disorder.
lead: Mirror checking and mirror avoidance are two opposite behavioral patterns around reflective surfaces that are described in body dysmorphic disorder (BDD). Wikipedia lists repetitive checking of one's appearance as a characteristic behavior of BDD and notes that some people instead avoid mirrors.

name: Reassurance seeking (rate me threads)
summary: Posting photos to be rated; the clinical analogue is reassurance seeking in BDD.
lead: Reassurance seeking, in the clinical sense, is frequently asking others for verbal confirmation about one's appearance. Wikipedia lists it among the repetitive behaviors of body dysmorphic disorder (BDD), alongside mirror checking, comparing and camouflaging.

name: Blackpill
summary: Fatalistic incel-born framework holding that looks and genetics set outcomes; debated inside looksmaxxing.
lead: The blackpill is a fatalistic worldview that originated on incel forums as a more nihilistic version of the manosphere's 'red pill'. It holds that dating and social outcomes are largely determined by physical attractiveness and genetics, and that men seen as unattractive cannot meaningfully change their position.
claims: Looks largely determine dating and social outcomes.
The blackpill is coping by insecure men.

name: Redpill / bluepill / purplepill frameworks
summary: Matrix-derived color metaphors for worldviews on dating and status; the black pill is the looks-deterministic one.
lead: The 'pill' frameworks are color-coded metaphors, borrowed from the 1999 film The Matrix, that online communities use to describe worldviews about dating, gender and social status. In the film, a red pill lets the character Neo see reality and a blue pill returns him to blissful ignorance.

name: Lookism
summary: Discrimination or judgement based on appearance, both an academic concept and core looksmaxxing vocabulary; research reports real but variable effects.
lead: Lookism is prejudice or discrimination against people judged physically unattractive, and also the tendency to infer someone's abilities or character from their appearance. It is studied in sociology, economics and psychology and is discussed in hiring, dating, politics and healthcare.
claims: Most people like or dislike you mainly because of your looks.
Being born less attractive makes people worth less to others.
Looksmaxxing forums help men cope with lookism.

name: Hardmaxxing
summary: Looksmaxxing slang for invasive appearance changes such as surgery, injectables and off-label drugs; established procedures exist, but DIY and fringe variants carry documented risks.
lead: Hardmaxxing is looksmaxxing slang for invasive or medically intensive methods of changing appearance, as opposed to 'softmaxxing', which covers non-invasive practices such as skincare, grooming, clothing and fitness.
claims: Surgery and medical procedures can substantially change facial structure.
Peptides and research chemicals add to hardmaxxing results for bones, skin and hair.
Bonesmashing is a form of hardmaxxing.
